D.t: David Jolly trails by 3.3 and wins 28% of simulations. Closing it takes about 148,442 voters switching sides, or 296,884 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.1 and D +4.8. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +4.9. Your best recent poll is Change Research at D +0.8; your worst is YouGov for N+ Univision at R +9.1. 15 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Broward, a projected net 230,430 votes; Orange, a projected net 122,438 votes; Palm Beach, a projected net 82,851 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Miami-Dade, R +0.1, 9.5% of the vote; Hillsborough, D +8.8, 6.3% of the vote; Pinellas, D +8.2, 5.1% of the vote; Duval, D +9.0, 4.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, David Jolly runs furthest behind in Collier, Okaloosa, Clay. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 79% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.96 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 67% of voters, 46 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.35 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 51 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.12 points.
The forecast's worst groups for David Jolly: Immigration voters 19 to 78, White voters 37 to 62, Midsize counties 39 to 59. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.0M cash against $44.0M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
